hero.label: Drug biography · No. 002
hero.line: Herceptin's antibody, given a chemotherapy payload to carry, and a new chance for people with very little HER2. Told in dated, sourced chapters.
hero.spec: HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate · first FDA approval Dec 20, 2019 · brand: Enhertu

chapters.title: Built on Herceptin
chapters.line: Enhertu starts with Herceptin's antibody, then gives it a chemotherapy payload to carry.
body: Enhertu's antibody has the same amino-acid sequence as trastuzumab, the antibody Genentech created and the FDA first approved as Herceptin in 1998. Daiichi Sankyo designed Enhertu and later developed it together with AstraZeneca.

Daiichi Sankyo attached a chemotherapy drug, deruxtecan (DXd), through a linker that is cut once the drug is inside the cell. Each antibody carries about 8 drug molecules, compared with about 3.5 for Kadcyla, the earlier trastuzumab-based conjugate, and the released drug can also reach neighboring cancer cells.
stat: drug molecules carried by each antibody, vs about 3.5 for Kadcyla

chapters.title: A $6.9 billion partner
chapters.line: AstraZeneca paid $1.35 billion up front to co-develop the drug with Daiichi Sankyo.
body: On March 28, 2019, Daiichi Sankyo and AstraZeneca announced a global agreement to develop and sell trastuzumab deruxtecan, then called DS-8201. AstraZeneca paid $1.35 billion up front, with milestone payments that could bring the total to $6.9 billion.
The two companies agreed to share costs and profits equally worldwide, with Daiichi Sankyo keeping exclusive rights in Japan.
stat: potential value of the AstraZeneca agreement

chapters.title: Approved, nine months later
chapters.line: The FDA granted accelerated approval for metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer.
body: On December 20, 2019, the FDA granted Enhertu accelerated approval for HER2-positive breast cancer that could not be removed by surgery or had spread, in people who had already received at least two HER2-targeted treatments.
That was about nine months after the AstraZeneca agreement.
stat: earlier HER2 treatments needed before Enhertu, under the first approval

chapters.title: Head to head with Kadcyla
chapters.line: In DESTINY-Breast03, Enhertu kept the cancer from growing far longer than Kadcyla, with a cost to the lungs.
body: DESTINY-Breast03 randomly assigned 524 people with metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer to Enhertu or Kadcyla. After 12 months, 75.8% on Enhertu were alive without their cancer growing, compared with 34.1% on Kadcyla, and Enhertu became the standard second treatment.

There was a cost. Drug-related lung inflammation (interstitial lung disease) affected about 10.5% of people on Enhertu and 1.9% on Kadcyla, mostly mild. Across nine trials, most cases were low grade, but some were severe and a small number were fatal.

chapters.title: A new group of patients
chapters.line: Enhertu worked even in tumors with only a little HER2, a group called HER2-low.
body: Until then, HER2 drugs were only for HER2-positive cancer. DESTINY-Breast04 tested Enhertu in 557 people whose metastatic cancer had low levels of HER2. Median survival was 23.4 months with Enhertu and 16.8 months with chemotherapy.
On August 6, 2022 the FDA approved Enhertu for HER2-low breast cancer, the first HER2-directed treatment for this group.

chapters.title: Beyond the breast
chapters.line: The FDA approved Enhertu for HER2-positive solid tumors of any type.
body: On April 5, 2024 the FDA granted accelerated approval for adults with HER2-positive (IHC 3+) solid tumors that had spread or could not be removed, after earlier treatment, and with no good alternatives.
It was the first antibody-drug conjugate, and the first HER2-directed treatment, approved by tumor marker rather than by where the cancer started.
stat: antibody-drug conjugate approved for any HER2-positive solid tumor

chapters.title: Even less HER2
chapters.line: Approval widened again, to tumors with barely detectable HER2.
body: DESTINY-Breast06 enrolled 866 people with hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer whose tumors were HER2-low or HER2-ultralow. Median time without the cancer growing was 13.2 months with Enhertu and 8.1 months with chemotherapy, and the benefit held for HER2-ultralow tumors.
In January 2025 the FDA approved Enhertu for HER2-low or HER2-ultralow metastatic breast cancer.

chapters.title: Moving earlier
chapters.line: Enhertu was approved for early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer, before and after surgery.
body: In DESTINY-Breast05, 1,635 people with HER2-positive early breast cancer that remained after initial treatment got Enhertu or Kadcyla after surgery. At three years, 92.4% on Enhertu were free of invasive disease, compared with 83.7% on Kadcyla. Lung inflammation affected 9.6% on Enhertu.
In May 2026 the FDA approved Enhertu for two new uses in HER2-positive early breast cancer, before and after surgery.
